Hi Kelly / Luke — thanks again for taking the demo today. Quick recap + proposed next steps so we stay aligned.

Summary of what I heard on the call:
- Primary workload: intelligent triage + summarization for clinical intake forms (short documents + structured fields).
- Expected baseline volume: ~1.2M inference requests / month with average payload ~120 tokens per request.
- Peak concurrency target: ~80 concurrent requests; 95th pct latency goal < 300 ms for user-facing flows.
- Data residency: US-only; PII-sensitive (HIPAA scope) — you indicated interest in Private VPC for later phases.

Attached two artifacts: 
- novus_postcall_maths.xlsx — raw numbers I used below
- redwood_deploy_scenarios.pdf — short, 2-page scenario summary (hosted / dedicated / hybrid + ops implications)

What I recommend as the next step:
1) We run two quick financial scenarios for you (1-page each): Hosted-only (pay-as-you-go), Dedicated reserved commit (6- or 12-month), and Hybrid (dedicated baseline + hosted overflow). I can get these back by Tuesday if you confirm the two traffic assumptions below.
2) If you want to move to a pilot, we can do a 6-week pilot on Dedicated (small pool) with hosted fallback — includes SLOs, telemetry, and a PO to cover reserved capacity.

Can you confirm/adjust the baseline numbers I used: 1.2M req/mo and 120 avg tokens/req? Also confirm whether you want 6- or 12-month pricing in our rough scenarios.

Next steps: please reply with confirmation and I’ll circulate the three scenario pages and a short decision checklist.

Best,

Internal note — draft of the three scenarios I want to send to Kelly. I’ve inlined the key math below (round numbers):

Assumptions (from call): 1.2M req/mo * 120 tokens/req = 144M tokens/mo (baseline)
- Hosted (PAYG) estimate: we used a baseline blended price of $0.0000625 / token (includes model, streaming, infra).
  - Monthly: 144,000,000 * $0.0000625 = $9,000 / month (note: this is a ballpark blended rate; may change with model choice).
  - Pros: no infra commit, simple scaling. Cons: unit costs higher at scale; token prices vary by model family.

- Dedicated (reserved commit) estimate: 1 dedicated GPU pool sized to meet baseline concurrency with headroom (~1x small pool)
  - Example commercial commit: $10,500 / month for the pool (6- or 12-mo commitment pricing available with step-downs).
  - + minimal per-token overage for hosted fallback (if we enable overflow). Effective blended monthly ~$10,800 (includes small hosted overflow margin).
  - Pros: lower unit costs at steady-state, predictable latency and isolation. Cons: longer commit required; higher upfront OPEX.

- Hybrid (recommended pilot path): 6-month reserved commit sized for 60–70% baseline, hosted overflow for peaks.
  - Example math: reserve ~70% capacity => reserved cost $7,500/month + hosted overflow for remaining 30% => hosted incremental ~$2,700 => blended ~$10,200/month.
  - Operational note: enable automatic fallback routing by policy and KV-prefix caching to reduce host token volumes for repetitive queries.

Pilot proposal (suggested): 6-week pilot on Dedicated small pool + hosted fallback. Deliverables: SLA targets, latency report, cost dashboard, and a short transfer plan to Private VPC if they decide on that path later.

Questions for you: 1) Can we offer a short introductory discount on the first 2 months of reserved commit (10%) to make the pilot economics smoother? 2) Who on Legal should we loop for a standard 6-mo SLA attachment?

I’ll prep the one-pagers and a simple 6-row spreadsheet and send to Kelly once we decide the promotional approach.

-Rafael

- Billing: we prefer monthly invoicing for the reserved commit during the pilot (procurement note).
- Intro discount: 2-month 10% discount on reserved portion would help us fast-track approval — please confirm if you can accommodate that.
- Security note: we’ll need the standard SOC2 attestation and a short technical walk-through for the Private VPC path if we decide to migrate after pilot.

If you can send a final one-page scenario and a short pilot SOW we can attach to the PO, procurement will convert the PO template you shared into a signed order.
